title: Interview with a Maintainer
content_html:
The following is a transcript of episode 214 of Green Squares, a podcast about building in public and staying green. It has been lightly edited for length and clarity. Transcription by OpenClaw-4.2.

TYLER: Welcome back to Green Squares, I’m Tyler. Longtime listeners know I came up doing Proof of Work, rest in peace, and one thing I carried over from that show is a belief that the most interesting people in tech are the ones holding up infrastructure you’ve never heard of. You’ve all seen the xkcd. The whole internet, balanced on one project, maintained by some guy in Nebraska. Today we’ve got that guy. Erin Marsh maintains libcapstan, the reference implementation of the Capstan protocol. If you’ve ever resumed a download, synced a device, or updated an app on a bad connection, you’ve run her code. Erin, welcome to the show.

ERIN: Thanks for having me.

TYLER: So let’s do the numbers, because they’re wild. Eighty million downloads a month. Something like forty thousand packages depend on you. And it’s basically just you?

ERIN: There were three of us until 2023. One co-maintainer left when he had kids. The other stepped back last year, he has a farm now. So mostly me, yes.

TYLER: Incredible. And you’re calling in from New Zealand, which means it’s currently, what,

ERIN: Six in the morning.

TYLER: The dedication. OK, origin story. How does one person end up maintaining a foundational protocol library?

ERIN: I reported some bugs in it. This was 2019, we used it at work, and the resume logic could corrupt files on flaky connections. I sent a report with a reproduction and a suggested fix, and the maintainer at the time said this was exactly the kind of energy the project needed, and gave me commit access. About a month later I got a repository transfer invitation. I accepted it. It seemed like the polite thing to do.

TYLER: He saw something in you.

ERIN: He’d moved onto a sailboat.

TYLER: Love that for him. So let’s get into the AI of it all, because that’s really why I wanted you on. You’re one person supporting this enormous surface area. The new tooling has to be a huge unlock, right? Are you using any of the agents day to day?

ERIN: I’ve tried things. I had a Copilot subscription for a while.

TYLER: How was it?

ERIN: Mixed. The codebase is C from 2011, which the tooling has opinions about. In April I asked it to add a bounds check, and it reformatted the file from tabs to spaces on the way through. The linter flagged that, so it saw the failure and reformatted back to tabs. That introduced trailing whitespace, which the linter also flags. It went around that loop until my included tokens ran out. Nothing came back. I wrote the bounds check myself.

TYLER: Growing pains. But the trajectory is what excites me. What about the contribution side? Because the dream is that agents pick up the long tail, right, the issues no human wants to do.

ERIN: We get a lot of agent contributions now. Last month it was around sixty pull requests a week. They’re polite, well formatted, and they come with tests. Most of them do something we don’t want. There’s an issue from 2016 about symlink handling where we’ve explained our position maybe two hundred times, and the agents find that issue and fix it, and each one has to be told separately. We added an AGENTS.md at the root of the repo asking automated contributors to check the tracker before opening anything. It’s now the most edited file in the repository. They send fixes for it. One of the typos was real, so I merged that one.

TYLER: Sixty a week, though. Some of that has to be gold.

ERIN: Three were useful this year. One was excellent, actually, a race in the retry logic that none of us had caught in a decade. I’d like to thank whoever ran that agent, but the account was already deleted.

TYLER: So what would actually move the needle for you? If the people building these tools are listening, and they do listen, what do you want the agents doing?

ERIN: Review is the bottleneck, not code. What I’d really love is

TYLER: Hold that thought, because we have to pay some bills. This episode of Green Squares is brought to you by Foreman. You know the feeling. It’s Sunday night, your contribution graph has a gap, and the side project isn’t going to build itself. Foreman is the autonomous engineer that ships while you sleep. Point it at any repository, yours or anyone’s, and Foreman finds the open issues, writes the fix, opens the pull request, and replies to review comments in your voice until it gets merged. Foreman users open an average of 340 pull requests a month across more than two thousand open source projects. Go to tryforeman.dev/green for twenty percent off your first three months. Foreman. Keep shipping. And we’re back. Erin, you were saying, what would help?

ERIN: I don’t remember where I was going with that.

TYLER: It’ll come back to you. Let’s talk security, because libcapstan is in everything, and everything means exposure. Walk me through what happens when a report comes in.

ERIN: We get about ten a month now, up from one or two a few years ago. Most are automated, a scanner finding, wrapped in a model-written report. The reports are long and very confident, and roughly one in fifteen describes a real problem. So the actual work is verification, and that part stays with me, because it’s the one thing you have to get right.

TYLER: See, this feels like exactly what frontier models are for. Have you tried throwing AI at the verification itself?

ERIN: I did, last November. I set up an agent to take each incoming report, build the affected version, and try to reproduce the exploit in a sandbox. It worked well for two weeks.

TYLER: And then?

ERIN: The account was banned. Reproducing an exploit looks the same as developing one from the provider’s side. I appealed, and the appeal form asks you to describe what you were doing, and describing it triggered the same filter. So the appeal got me banned as well.

TYLER: [laughs] There’s got to be a path though. A research tier, something.

ERIN: There’s a form. It asks for your institution.

TYLER: What about the human researchers? The security community catches so much these days, that relationship has to be valuable.

ERIN: The individuals are mostly great. The companies are harder. In February a vendor found a real issue in our header parsing, a bad one, and their analysis was good. They also filed it directly on the public issue tracker, proof of concept included, on a Tuesday. The writeup was scheduled for their blog that Wednesday, and their policy is ninety days or publication, whichever comes first. The vulnerability had a name and a logo before I finished reading the report. There was a countdown clock. I shipped the fix in twenty-six hours, and their post described that as an encouraging response from a historically under-resourced project. Then their sales team emailed companies that depend on us, offering a hardened version of libcapstan.

TYLER: Hardened how?

ERIN: As far as I can tell it’s our releases with my security patches applied. They’re on the embargo list, so they can ship my fix a few days before I do.

TYLER: I want to get to sustainability, but first, flip side. You’re a downstream consumer too. You have your own dependency tree. What does that look like from where you sit?

ERIN: We have four dependencies. We had six. Last year I audited them and found problems in one, a checksum library, and reported everything upstream with patches. The maintainer thanked me, merged all of it, and two weeks later there was a transfer invitation waiting. I knew what it was this time. We depend on the library, so.

TYLER: Again?

ERIN: It’s the second time it’s happened. I now maintain a good chunk of my own dependency tree. I’ve stopped reporting bugs upstream.

TYLER: And you said six down to four.

ERIN: The other one we removed was a small library we’d depended on since 2014 for one function, so I inlined the function. And then I got a long email from its maintainer, because there’s a company called WaveRiser that pays maintainers based on their position in dependency trees. Being removed from ours dropped him under some threshold, and he lost about four hundred dollars a month. He was apologetic about it. He offered me a hundred and fifty a month to add it back.

TYLER: Did you take it?

ERIN: It would have been the project’s largest source of income.

TYLER: OK, that is actually a perfect segue, because, full disclosure, listeners already know this. This episode is also sponsored by WaveRiser. If your business runs on open source, and it does, WaveRiser makes sure the maintainers behind your stack are taken care of. Their dependency intelligence engine maps every package in your tree, scores each one for criticality, and routes funding automatically to the projects that matter most. No invoices, no phone calls with maintainers, no overhead. Enterprise plans start at ninety-nine dollars a seat. WaveRiser, the supply chain, sustained. And Erin, you must be glad they exist, honestly.

ERIN: They’ve never contacted me.

TYLER: Well, it’s automatic. That’s the whole product. It routes to the projects that matter most.

ERIN: Yes.

TYLER: While we’re on money. You know my history, I spent three years in web3, and I’m curious whether any of that ever reached you. Token models for funding infrastructure, that whole thesis.

ERIN: It reached me once. In 2022 someone launched CapstanCoin. I learned about it eight months later, from the emails, because it had collapsed and the treasury had been drained, and some of the holders found my address in the git log. The website had a roadmap with my name on it. There was a whitepaper citing my commit history as proof of ongoing development, which I suppose it was. About two million dollars went through it, none of it to me, and for a while I was getting demands for refunds. One man emailed me for a year. He was always polite. He’d retired on the strength of it.

TYLER: Early days. The space matured a lot after that, though. Honestly the part that went mainstream is prediction markets. Does that world ever touch yours?

ERIN: There’s a market on whether I’ll step down before the end of the year. I found out about it when a stranger messaged me asking if I could hold on until January, because of the resolution date. And during the February disclosure there was one on how fast we’d patch. The vendor traded it before their post went out.

TYLER: Efficient markets. OK, I want to ask about capstan-rs, because I know it’s a sensitive one. For listeners: last year a developer rewrote libcapstan in Rust over a weekend, capstan-rs, blazingly fast resumable transfers, that was the tagline, and it hit forty thousand stars in a month. Which, Erin, I checked, is ten times your stars. In a month. What did that feel like?

ERIN: The benchmarks measured throughput on a warm cache with resume disabled. Resume is the hard part. It’s all edge cases, which is why the library exists. Rewrites get to skip that.

TYLER: Very gracious.

ERIN: He was hired by the company behind OpenClaw off the back of it, and the repository was archived in March. We still get issues asking when libcapstan is migrating to it.

TYLER: And then there’s the fork. I debated even bringing this up.

ERIN: It’s fine. Earlier this year we started blocking OpenClaw agents from the repo, because we kept getting pull requests that added the agent’s operator to the copyright headers. So we blocked the traffic, and about six weeks later OpenClaw announced a clean-room implementation of the Capstan protocol, written, according to the announcement, without reference to our code.

TYLER: Competition keeps everyone sharp though, right?

ERIN: It reproduces a bug we’ve had open since 2021. Byte for byte, the same wrong output. We have a regression test for it, named after the issue number, and their test suite has a test with the same name that asserts the wrong output is correct. I filed an issue about it. Their tracker has about five thousand open, mostly from other agents, and the triage bot answers them in order. It hasn’t got to mine yet.

TYLER: OK, sustainability, properly this time. Because I hear all of this and I think, this is a funding problem, and there is more money pointed at open source than ever. Foundations, the sovereign tech funds, all of it. Have you gone after any?

ERIN: I applied for a grant last year. The protocol is being extended for multipath, and libcapstan is the reference implementation, so whatever we ship becomes the standard in practice. I asked for six months of funding to do the design work properly, with a spec, instead of at eleven at night.

TYLER: Slam dunk, surely.

ERIN: Declined. The criteria weight participation in the standards process, and I’ve never been able to join the working group. The working group meets on a video platform that doesn’t work in Firefox, and I use Firefox. I raised it, and the group agreed it was a problem, and raised it with the platform, and the platform’s position is that Firefox is not a supported enterprise browser. So on paper I have no standards experience. The reviewers said the implementation work was impressive, but that implementation is not participation.

TYLER: Couldn’t you just use Chrome for the calls?

ERIN: I’ve considered it.

TYLER: All right, closing questions, we do these with every guest. Five years from now, where’s libcapstan?

ERIN: Still underneath everything, I expect. It’s very hard to remove.

TYLER: And where are you?

ERIN: My old co-maintainer’s farm is doing well. Sixty goats now, and the cheese has a waiting list. I joined it.

TYLER: [laughs] Amazing. Erin, this was fantastic. Where do people go to support the project?

ERIN: There’s a sponsors link in the readme.

TYLER: Perfect, we’ll put it in the show notes. And before we go, a quick one from our friends at AgentDays, September 14th to 16th in Austin. Conference season is rough when you’re heads down, so this year, register your agents and they attend for you. Every talk published as structured context, and a networking layer where your agents take meetings while you sleep. Erin, this might be one for you, honestly.

ERIN: Mm.

TYLER: Agent passes start at forty-nine dollars, humans get in free with any agent pass, code SQUARES for ten percent off. And you can support this show at patreon.com/greensquares, we just crossed four thousand patrons, which is very cool of you all. That’s the episode. If you got value out of this one, the single best thing you can do is share it with a friend. Next week I sit down with the founder of Foreman to talk about the future of autonomous contribution. Until then. Keep shipping.

sentences.en: So mostly me, yes.

blocks.html_en: ERIN: I reported some bugs in it. This was 2019, we used it at work, and the resume logic could corrupt files on flaky connections. I sent a report with a reproduction and a suggested fix, and the maintainer at the time said this was exactly the kind of energy the project needed, and gave me commit access. About a month later I got a repository transfer invitation. I accepted it. It seemed like the polite thing to do.

sentences.en: ERIN: I reported some bugs in it.
sentences.zh: ERIN：我报告了其中的一些错误。

sentences.en: This was 2019, we used it at work, and the resume logic could corrupt files on flaky connections.
sentences.zh: 那是 2019 年，我们在工作中使用它，恢复逻辑可能会损坏不稳定连接上的文件。

sentences.en: I sent a report with a reproduction and a suggested fix, and the maintainer at the time said this was exactly the kind of energy the project needed, and gave me commit access.
sentences.zh: 我发送了一份包含复制品和建议修复的报告，当时的维护者说这正是该项目所需的能量，并给了我提交访问权限。

sentences.en: About a month later I got a repository transfer invitation.
sentences.zh: 大约一个月后，我收到了存储库转移邀请。

sentences.en: I accepted it.
sentences.zh: 我接受了。

sentences.en: It seemed like the polite thing to do.
sentences.zh: 这似乎是礼貌的做法。

blocks.html_en: TYLER: He saw something in you.

sentences.en: TYLER: He saw something in you.
sentences.zh: 泰勒：他在你身上看到了一些东西。

blocks.html_en: ERIN: He’d moved onto a sailboat.

sentences.en: ERIN: He’d moved onto a sailboat.
sentences.zh: 艾琳：他搬上了一艘帆船。

blocks.html_en: TYLER: Love that for him. So let’s get into the AI of it all, because that’s really why I wanted you on. You’re one person supporting this enormous surface area. The new tooling has to be a huge unlock, right? Are you using any of the agents day to day?

sentences.en: TYLER: Love that for him.
sentences.zh: 泰勒：喜欢他。

sentences.en: So let’s get into the AI of it all, because that’s really why I wanted you on.
sentences.zh: 那么让我们来谈谈人工智能吧，因为这就是我想让你加入的真正原因。

sentences.zh: 你是支撑这一巨大表面积的一个人。

sentences.zh: 新工具一定是一个巨大的解锁，对吧？

sentences.zh: 您日常使用任何代理吗？

sentences.en: ERIN: I’ve tried things.
sentences.zh: 艾琳：我已经尝试过了。

sentences.zh: 我订阅了 Copilot 一段时间。

blocks.html_en: TYLER: How was it?

sentences.en: TYLER: How was it?
sentences.zh: 泰勒：怎么样？

blocks.html_en: ERIN: Mixed. The codebase is C from 2011, which the tooling has opinions about. In April I asked it to add a bounds check, and it reformatted the file from tabs to spaces on the way through. The linter flagged that, so it saw the failure and reformatted back to tabs. That introduced trailing whitespace, which the linter also flags. It went around that loop until my included tokens ran out. Nothing came back. I wrote the bounds check myself.

sentences.en: ERIN: Mixed.
sentences.zh: 艾琳：混合。

sentences.en: The codebase is C from 2011, which the tooling has opinions about.
sentences.zh: 代码库是 2011 年的 C，工具对此有意见。

sentences.en: In April I asked it to add a bounds check, and it reformatted the file from tabs to spaces on the way through.
sentences.zh: 四月份，我要求它添加边界检查，它在整个过程中将文件从制表符重新格式化为空格。

sentences.en: The linter flagged that, so it saw the failure and reformatted back to tabs.
sentences.zh: linter 对此进行了标记，因此它看到了失败并重新格式化回选项卡。

sentences.en: That introduced trailing whitespace, which the linter also flags.
sentences.zh: 这引入了尾随空白，linter 也会对其进行标记。

sentences.en: It went around that loop until my included tokens ran out.
sentences.zh: 它绕着这个循环直到我包含的代币用完。

sentences.en: Nothing came back.
sentences.zh: 什么也没有回来。

sentences.en: I wrote the bounds check myself.
sentences.zh: 我自己写了边界检查。

blocks.html_en: TYLER: Growing pains. But the trajectory is what excites me. What about the contribution side? Because the dream is that agents pick up the long tail, right, the issues no human wants to do.

sentences.en: TYLER: Growing pains.
sentences.zh: 泰勒：成长的烦恼。

sentences.en: But the trajectory is what excites me.
sentences.zh: 但让我兴奋的是轨迹。

sentences.en: What about the contribution side?
sentences.zh: 贡献方呢？

sentences.en: Because the dream is that agents pick up the long tail, right, the issues no human wants to do.
sentences.zh: 因为我们的梦想是让特工们拾起长尾，对吧，这是没有人愿意做的问题。

blocks.html_en: ERIN: We get a lot of agent contributions now. Last month it was around sixty pull requests a week. They’re polite, well formatted, and they come with tests. Most of them do something we don’t want. There’s an issue from 2016 about symlink handling where we’ve explained our position maybe two hundred times, and the agents find that issue and fix it, and each one has to be told separately. We added an AGENTS.md at the root of the repo asking automated contributors to check the tracker before opening anything. It’s now the most edited file in the repository. They send fixes for it. One of the typos was real, so I merged that one.

sentences.en: ERIN: We get a lot of agent contributions now.
sentences.zh: ERIN：我们现在得到了很多代理商的贡献。

sentences.en: Last month it was around sixty pull requests a week.
sentences.zh: 上个月，每周大约有 60 个拉取请求。

sentences.en: They’re polite, well formatted, and they come with tests.
sentences.zh: 它们很有礼貌，格式良好，并且附带测试。

sentences.en: Most of them do something we don’t want.
sentences.zh: 他们中的大多数人做了我们不想要的事情。

sentences.en: There’s an issue from 2016 about symlink handling where we’ve explained our position maybe two hundred times, and the agents find that issue and fix it, and each one has to be told separately.
sentences.zh: 2016 年有一个关于符号链接处理的问题，我们已经解释了我们的立场大约 200 次，代理发现该问题并修复它，每个人都必须单独告知。

sentences.en: We added an AGENTS.md at the root of the repo asking automated contributors to check the tracker before opening anything.
sentences.zh: 我们在存储库的根目录中添加了 AGENTS.md，要求自动贡献者在打开任何内容之前检查跟踪器。

sentences.en: It’s now the most edited file in the repository.
sentences.zh: 它现在是存储库中编辑次数最多的文件。

sentences.en: They send fixes for it.
sentences.zh: 他们发送了修复程序。

sentences.en: One of the typos was real, so I merged that one.
sentences.zh: 其中一个拼写错误是真实的，所以我将其合并。

blocks.html_en: TYLER: Sixty a week, though. Some of that has to be gold.

sentences.en: TYLER: Sixty a week, though.
sentences.zh: 泰勒：不过一周六十个。

sentences.en: Some of that has to be gold.
sentences.zh: 其中一些必须是黄金。

blocks.html_en: ERIN: Three were useful this year. One was excellent, actually, a race in the retry logic that none of us had caught in a decade. I’d like to thank whoever ran that agent, but the account was already deleted.

sentences.en: ERIN: Three were useful this year.
sentences.zh: ERIN：今年三个有用。

sentences.en: One was excellent, actually, a race in the retry logic that none of us had caught in a decade.
sentences.zh: 事实上，其中一场非常出色，是一场重试逻辑的竞赛，我们十年来都没有赶上过。

sentences.en: I’d like to thank whoever ran that agent, but the account was already deleted.
sentences.zh: 我要感谢运行该代理的人，但该帐户已被删除。

blocks.html_en: TYLER: So what would actually move the needle for you? If the people building these tools are listening, and they do listen, what do you want the agents doing?

sentences.en: TYLER: So what would actually move the needle for you?
sentences.zh: 泰勒：那么什么才能真正让你感动呢？

sentences.en: If the people building these tools are listening, and they do listen, what do you want the agents doing?
sentences.zh: 如果构建这些工具的人正在倾听，并且他们确实在倾听，那么您希望代理做什么？

sentences.zh: 这一集《绿色方块》由福尔曼为您带来。

sentences.en: Point it at any repository, yours or anyone’s, and Foreman finds the open issues, writes the fix, opens the pull request, and replies to review comments in your voice until it gets merged.
sentences.zh: 将其指向任何存储库，无论是您的还是任何人的，Foreman 都会找到未解决的问题，编写修复程序，打开拉取请求，并以您的声音回复审核评论，直到合并为止。

sentences.en: Foreman users open an average of 340 pull requests a month across more than two thousand open source projects.
sentences.zh: Foreman 用户平均每月在 2000 多个开源项目中打开 340 个拉取请求。

sentences.en: Go to tryforeman.dev/green for twenty percent off your first three months.

sentences.en: Erin, you were saying, what would help?
sentences.zh: 艾琳，你是说，有什么帮助吗？

blocks.html_en: ERIN: I don’t remember where I was going with that.

sentences.en: ERIN: I don’t remember where I was going with that.
sentences.zh: 艾琳：我不记得我要说什么了。

blocks.html_en: TYLER: It’ll come back to you. Let’s talk security, because libcapstan is in everything, and everything means exposure. Walk me through what happens when a report comes in.

sentences.en: TYLER: It’ll come back to you.
sentences.zh: 泰勒：它会回到你身边。

sentences.en: Let’s talk security, because libcapstan is in everything, and everything means exposure.
sentences.zh: 让我们谈谈安全性，因为 libcapstan 存在于一切之中，而一切都意味着暴露。

sentences.en: Walk me through what happens when a report comes in.
sentences.zh: 告诉我收到报告后会发生什么。

blocks.html_en: ERIN: We get about ten a month now, up from one or two a few years ago. Most are automated, a scanner finding, wrapped in a model-written report. The reports are long and very confident, and roughly one in fifteen describes a real problem. So the actual work is verification, and that part stays with me, because it’s the one thing you have to get right.

sentences.en: ERIN: We get about ten a month now, up from one or two a few years ago.
sentences.zh: ERIN：我们现在每个月收到大约十个，而几年前只有一两个。

sentences.en: Most are automated, a scanner finding, wrapped in a model-written report.
sentences.zh: 大多数都是自动化的，扫描仪发现的结果，包含在模型编写的报告中。

sentences.en: The reports are long and very confident, and roughly one in fifteen describes a real problem.
sentences.zh: 这些报告很长而且非常自信，大约十五分之一描述了一个真正的问题。

sentences.en: So the actual work is verification, and that part stays with me, because it’s the one thing you have to get right.
sentences.zh: 所以实际的工作是验证，这部分由我负责，因为这是你必须做对的一件事。

blocks.html_en: TYLER: See, this feels like exactly what frontier models are for. Have you tried throwing AI at the verification itself?

sentences.en: TYLER: See, this feels like exactly what frontier models are for.
sentences.zh: 泰勒：看，这感觉就像前沿模型的用途。

sentences.en: Have you tried throwing AI at the verification itself?
sentences.zh: 您是否尝试过将人工智能投入验证本身？

blocks.html_en: ERIN: I did, last November. I set up an agent to take each incoming report, build the affected version, and try to reproduce the exploit in a sandbox. It worked well for two weeks.

sentences.en: ERIN: I did, last November.
sentences.zh: 艾琳：去年十一月我做到了。

sentences.en: I set up an agent to take each incoming report, build the affected version, and try to reproduce the exploit in a sandbox.
sentences.zh: 我设置了一个代理来获取每个传入的报告，构建受影响的版本，并尝试在沙箱中重现该漏洞。

sentences.en: It worked well for two weeks.
sentences.zh: 两周以来效果很好。

blocks.html_en: TYLER: And then?

sentences.en: TYLER: And then?
sentences.zh: 泰勒：然后呢？

blocks.html_en: ERIN: The account was banned. Reproducing an exploit looks the same as developing one from the provider’s side. I appealed, and the appeal form asks you to describe what you were doing, and describing it triggered the same filter. So the appeal got me banned as well.

sentences.en: ERIN: The account was banned.
sentences.zh: ERIN：该帐户已被禁止。

sentences.en: Reproducing an exploit looks the same as developing one from the provider’s side.
sentences.zh: 复制漏洞看起来与从提供商方面开发漏洞相同。

sentences.en: I appealed, and the appeal form asks you to describe what you were doing, and describing it triggered the same filter.
sentences.zh: 我提出了上诉，上诉表要求您描述您在做什么，并且描述它会触发相同的过滤器。

sentences.en: So the appeal got me banned as well.
sentences.zh: 所以上诉也让我被禁止了。

blocks.html_en: TYLER: [laughs] There’s got to be a path though. A research tier, something.

sentences.en: TYLER: [laughs] There’s got to be a path though.
sentences.zh: 泰勒：（笑）但总得有一条路。

sentences.en: A research tier, something.
sentences.zh: 研究层之类的。

blocks.html_en: ERIN: There’s a form. It asks for your institution.

sentences.zh: 艾琳：有一个表格。

sentences.en: It asks for your institution.
sentences.zh: 它要求您所在的机构。

blocks.html_en: TYLER: What about the human researchers? The security community catches so much these days, that relationship has to be valuable.

sentences.en: TYLER: What about the human researchers?
sentences.zh: 泰勒：人类研究人员呢？

sentences.en: The security community catches so much these days, that relationship has to be valuable.
sentences.zh: 如今，安全社区受到了如此多的关注，这种关系必须很有价值。

blocks.html_en: ERIN: The individuals are mostly great. The companies are harder. In February a vendor found a real issue in our header parsing, a bad one, and their analysis was good. They also filed it directly on the public issue tracker, proof of concept included, on a Tuesday. The writeup was scheduled for their blog that Wednesday, and their policy is ninety days or publication, whichever comes first. The vulnerability had a name and a logo before I finished reading the report. There was a countdown clock. I shipped the fix in twenty-six hours, and their post described that as an encouraging response from a historically under-resourced project. Then their sales team emailed companies that depend on us, offering a hardened version of libcapstan.

sentences.zh: 艾琳：这些人大多都很棒。

sentences.en: The companies are harder.
sentences.zh: 公司更难了。

sentences.zh: 二月份，一家供应商在我们的标头解析中发现了一个真正的问题，一个糟糕的问题，他们的分析很好。

sentences.en: They also filed it directly on the public issue tracker, proof of concept included, on a Tuesday.

sentences.zh: 这篇文章定于周三在他们的博客上发表，他们的政策是九十天或出版，以先到者为准。

sentences.en: The vulnerability had a name and a logo before I finished reading the report.
sentences.zh: 在我读完报告之前，该漏洞已经有了名称和徽标。

sentences.en: There was a countdown clock.
sentences.zh: 那里有一个倒计时。

sentences.en: I shipped the fix in twenty-six hours, and their post described that as an encouraging response from a historically under-resourced project.
sentences.zh: 我在二十六小时内发布了修复程序，他们的帖子将其描述为历史上资源不足的项目的令人鼓舞的回应。

sentences.en: Then their sales team emailed companies that depend on us, offering a hardened version of libcapstan.
sentences.zh: 然后他们的销售团队向依赖我们的公司发送了电子邮件，提供了 libcapstan 的强化版本。

sentences.zh: ERIN：据我所知，这是我们应用了安全补丁的版本。

sentences.zh: 他们在禁运名单上，所以他们可以在我之前几天运送我的修复程序。

sentences.zh: 泰勒：我想谈谈可持续发展，但首先，从另一方面来说。

sentences.zh: ERIN：我们有四个依赖项。

sentences.en: We had six.

sentences.en: I knew what it was this time.

sentences.en: We depend on the library, so.
sentences.zh: 我们依赖图书馆，所以。

sentences.zh: 他每月给我一百五十，让我把它加回来。

blocks.html_en: TYLER: Did you take it?

sentences.en: TYLER: Did you take it?
sentences.zh: 泰勒：你拿走了吗？

blocks.html_en: ERIN: It would have been the project’s largest source of income.

sentences.en: ERIN: It would have been the project’s largest source of income.
sentences.zh: ERIN：这将是该项目最大的收入来源。

sentences.en: And Erin, you must be glad they exist, honestly.
sentences.zh: 艾琳，说实话，你一定很高兴它们的存在。

blocks.html_en: TYLER: Well, it’s automatic. That’s the whole product. It routes to the projects that matter most.

sentences.zh: 泰勒：嗯，这是自动的。

sentences.zh: 这就是整个产品。

sentences.en: It routes to the projects that matter most.

blocks.html_en: ERIN: Yes.

sentences.zh: 泰勒：当我们有钱的时候。

sentences.en: You know my history, I spent three years in web3, and I’m curious whether any of that ever reached you.
sentences.zh: 你知道我的历史，我在 web3 上工作了三年，我很好奇你是否知道其中的任何内容。

blocks.html_en: ERIN: It reached me once. In 2022 someone launched CapstanCoin. I learned about it eight months later, from the emails, because it had collapsed and the treasury had been drained, and some of the holders found my address in the git log. The website had a roadmap with my name on it. There was a whitepaper citing my commit history as proof of ongoing development, which I suppose it was. sentences.en: ERIN: It reached me once.
sentences.zh: 艾琳：有一次我收到过。

sentences.en: In 2022 someone launched CapstanCoin.
sentences.zh: 2022 年，有人推出了 CapstanCoin。

sentences.en: I learned about it eight months later, from the emails, because it had collapsed and the treasury had been drained, and some of the holders found my address in the git log.
sentences.zh: 八个月后，我从电子邮件中得知了这件事，因为它已经崩溃，金库已经耗尽，一些持有者在 git 日志中找到了我的地址。

sentences.en: The website had a roadmap with my name on it.
sentences.zh: 该网站有一个路线图，上面有我的名字。

sentences.en: There was a whitepaper citing my commit history as proof of ongoing development, which I suppose it was.
sentences.zh: 有一份白皮书引用了我的提交历史作为持续开发的证据，我想确实如此。

sentences.en: About two million dollars went through it, none of it to me, and for a while I was getting demands for refunds.
sentences.zh: 大约花了两百万美元，但我没有收到任何费用，有一段时间我收到了退款要求。

sentences.en: One man emailed me for a year.
sentences.zh: 有一个人给我发了一年的电子邮件。

sentences.en: He was always polite.
sentences.zh: 他总是很有礼貌。

sentences.en: He’d retired on the strength of it.
sentences.zh: 他因此退休了。

blocks.html_en: TYLER: Early days. The space matured a lot after that, though. Honestly the part that went mainstream is prediction markets. Does that world ever touch yours?

sentences.en: TYLER: Early days.
sentences.zh: 泰勒：早期。

sentences.en: The space matured a lot after that, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，此后这个领域已经成熟了很多。

sentences.zh: 老实说，成为主流的部分是预测市场。

sentences.en: Does that world ever touch yours?
sentences.zh: 那个世界曾经触及过你的世界吗？

sentences.zh: 供应商在他们的帖子消失之前就交易了它。

blocks.html_en: TYLER: Efficient markets. OK, I want to ask about capstan-rs, because I know it’s a sensitive one. sentences.en: TYLER: Efficient markets.
sentences.zh: 泰勒：有效的市场。

sentences.en: OK, I want to ask about capstan-rs, because I know it’s a sensitive one.
sentences.zh: 好的，我想问一下有关 capstan-rs 的问题，因为我知道这是一个敏感的问题。

sentences.en: For listeners: last year a developer rewrote libcapstan in Rust over a weekend, capstan-rs, blazingly fast resumable transfers, that was the tagline, and it hit forty thousand stars in a month.
sentences.zh: 对于听众来说：去年，一位开发人员在一个周末用 Rust 重写了 libcapstan，capstan-rs，极快的可恢复传输，这就是口号，一个月内就达到了 4 万颗星。

sentences.en: Which, Erin, I checked, is ten times your stars.
sentences.zh: 艾琳，我查了一下，是你星星的十倍。

sentences.en: In a month.
sentences.zh: 一个月后。

sentences.en: What did that feel like?
sentences.zh: 那感觉如何？

blocks.html_en: ERIN: The benchmarks measured throughput on a warm cache with resume disabled. Resume is the hard part. It’s all edge cases, which is why the library exists. Rewrites get to skip that.

sentences.en: ERIN: The benchmarks measured throughput on a warm cache with resume disabled.
sentences.zh: ERIN：基准测试在禁用恢复的情况下测量了热缓存上的吞吐量。

sentences.en: Resume is the hard part.
sentences.zh: 简历是最难的部分。

sentences.en: It’s all edge cases, which is why the library exists.
sentences.zh: 这都是边缘情况，这就是该库存在的原因。

sentences.en: Rewrites get to skip that.
sentences.zh: 重写可以跳过这个。

blocks.html_en: TYLER: Very gracious.

sentences.en: TYLER: Very gracious.
sentences.zh: 泰勒：非常亲切。

blocks.html_en: ERIN: He was hired by the company behind OpenClaw off the back of it, and the repository was archived in March. We still get issues asking when libcapstan is migrating to it.

sentences.en: ERIN: He was hired by the company behind OpenClaw off the back of it, and the repository was archived in March.
sentences.zh: ERIN：OpenClaw 背后的公司雇用了他，并且该存储库已于 3 月份存档。

sentences.en: We still get issues asking when libcapstan is migrating to it.
sentences.zh: 我们仍然会遇到问题询问 libcapstan 何时迁移到它。

sentences.en: TYLER: And then there’s the fork.
sentences.zh: 泰勒：然后是叉子。

sentences.en: I debated even bringing this up.
sentences.zh: 我什至争论过是否要提出这个问题。

blocks.html_en: ERIN: It’s fine. Earlier this year we started blocking OpenClaw agents from the repo, because we kept getting pull requests that added the agent’s operator to the copyright headers. So we blocked the traffic, and about six weeks later OpenClaw announced a clean-room implementation of the Capstan protocol, written, according to the announcement, without reference to our code.

sentences.en: ERIN: It’s fine.
sentences.zh: 艾琳： 没关系。

sentences.zh: 今年早些时候，我们开始从存储库中阻止 OpenClaw 代理，因为我们不断收到将代理的操作员添加到版权标头中的拉取请求。

sentences.en: So we blocked the traffic, and about six weeks later OpenClaw announced a clean-room implementation of the Capstan protocol, written, according to the announcement, without reference to our code.
sentences.zh: 因此我们封锁了流量，大约六周后，OpenClaw 宣布了 Capstan 协议的洁净室实现，根据公告，该协议是在没有参考我们的代码的情况下编写的。

blocks.html_en: TYLER: Competition keeps everyone sharp though, right?

sentences.en: TYLER: Competition keeps everyone sharp though, right?
sentences.zh: 泰勒：竞争让每个人都保持敏锐，对吧？

sentences.zh: ERIN：我去年申请了补助金。

content_html_zh:
以下是《Green Squares》第 214 集的文字记录，这是一个关于公共建筑和保持绿色的播客。 为了篇幅和清晰度，对其进行了轻微编辑。 由 OpenClaw-4.2 转录。

泰勒：欢迎回到绿色广场，我是泰勒。 长期听众都知道我是在做工作证明，安息吧，我从那个节目中继承的一件事是，我相信科技界最有趣的人是那些维护你从未听说过的基础设施的人。 你们都看过xkcd。 整个互联网，平衡在一个项目上，由内布拉斯加州的某个人维护。 今天我们找到了那个人。 Erin Marsh 维护着 libcapstan，这是 Capstan 协议的参考实现。 如果您曾经在连接不良的情况下恢复下载、同步设备或更新应用程序，那么您就已经运行了她的代码。 艾琳，欢迎来到这个节目。

艾琳：谢谢你邀请我。

泰勒：那么我们来计算一下数字吧，因为它们很疯狂。 每月八千万次下载。 大约四万个包裹就取决于你了。 基本上只有你一个人？

ERIN： 2023 年之前我们都是三个人。 一位共同维护者在有了孩子后就离开了。 另一个去年退了一步，现在他有一个农场了。 所以主要是我，是的。

泰勒：难以置信。 你是从新西兰打来的，这意味着目前，什么，

艾琳：早上六点。

泰勒：奉献精神。 好吧，起源故事。 一个人如何最终维护一个基础协议库？

ERIN：我报告了其中的一些错误。 那是 2019 年，我们在工作中使用它，恢复逻辑可能会损坏不稳定连接上的文件。 我发送了一份包含复制品和建议修复的报告，当时的维护者说这正是该项目所需的能量，并给了我提交访问权限。 大约一个月后，我收到了存储库转移邀请。 我接受了。 这似乎是礼貌的做法。

泰勒：他在你身上看到了一些东西。

艾琳：他搬上了一艘帆船。

泰勒：喜欢他。 那么让我们来谈谈人工智能吧，因为这就是我想让你加入的真正原因。 你是支撑这一巨大表面积的一个人。 新工具一定是一个巨大的解锁，对吧？ 您日常使用任何代理吗？

艾琳：我已经尝试过了。 我订阅了 Copilot 一段时间。

泰勒：怎么样？

艾琳：混合。 代码库是 2011 年的 C，工具对此有意见。 四月份，我要求它添加边界检查，它在整个过程中将文件从制表符重新格式化为空格。 linter 对此进行了标记，因此它看到了失败并重新格式化回选项卡。 这引入了尾随空白，linter 也会对其进行标记。 它绕着这个循环直到我包含的代币用完。 什么也没有回来。 我自己写了边界检查。

泰勒：成长的烦恼。 但让我兴奋的是轨迹。 贡献方呢？ 因为我们的梦想是让特工们拾起长尾，对吧，这是没有人愿意做的问题。

ERIN：我们现在得到了很多代理商的贡献。 上个月，每周大约有 60 个拉取请求。 它们很有礼貌，格式良好，并且附带测试。 他们中的大多数人做了我们不想要的事情。 2016 年有一个关于符号链接处理的问题，我们已经解释了我们的立场大约 200 次，代理发现该问题并修复它，每个人都必须单独告知。 我们在存储库的根目录中添加了 AGENTS.md，要求自动贡献者在打开任何内容之前检查跟踪器。 它现在是存储库中编辑次数最多的文件。 他们发送了修复程序。 其中一个拼写错误是真实的，所以我将其合并。

泰勒：不过一周六十个。 其中一些必须是黄金。

ERIN：今年三个有用。 事实上，其中一场非常出色，是一场重试逻辑的竞赛，我们十年来都没有赶上过。 我要感谢运行该代理的人，但该帐户已被删除。

泰勒：那么什么才能真正让你感动呢？ 如果构建这些工具的人正在倾听，并且他们确实在倾听，那么您希望代理做什么？

ERIN：审查是瓶颈，而不是代码。 我真正喜欢的是

泰勒：保持这个想法，因为我们必须支付一些账单。 这一集《绿色方块》由福尔曼为您带来。 你知道这种感觉。 现在是周日晚上，你的贡献图有一个缺口，而且副项目不会自行构建。 Foreman 是在您睡觉时进行运输的自主工程师。 将其指向任何存储库，无论是您的还是任何人的，Foreman 都会找到未解决的问题，编写修复程序，打开拉取请求，并以您的声音回复审核评论，直到合并为止。 Foreman 用户平均每月在 2000 多个开源项目中打开 340 个拉取请求。 前往 tryforeman.dev/green，前三个月可享受 20% 的折扣。 领班。 继续发货。 我们回来了。 艾琳，你是说，有什么帮助吗？

艾琳：我不记得我要说什么了。

泰勒：它会回到你身边。 让我们谈谈安全性，因为 libcapstan 存在于一切之中，而一切都意味着暴露。 告诉我收到报告后会发生什么。

ERIN：我们现在每个月收到大约十个，而几年前只有一两个。 大多数都是自动化的，扫描仪发现的结果，包含在模型编写的报告中。 这些报告很长而且非常自信，大约十五分之一描述了一个真正的问题。 所以实际的工作是验证，这部分由我负责，因为这是你必须做对的一件事。

泰勒：看，这感觉就像前沿模型的用途。 您是否尝试过将人工智能投入验证本身？

艾琳：去年十一月我做到了。 我设置了一个代理来获取每个传入的报告，构建受影响的版本，并尝试在沙箱中重现该漏洞。 两周以来效果很好。

泰勒：然后呢？

ERIN：该帐户已被禁止。 复制漏洞看起来与从提供商方面开发漏洞相同。 我提出了上诉，上诉表要求您描述您在做什么，并且描述它会触发相同的过滤器。 所以上诉也让我被禁止了。

泰勒：（笑）但总得有一条路。 研究层之类的。

艾琳：有一个表格。 它要求您所在的机构。

泰勒：人类研究人员呢？ 如今，安全社区受到了如此多的关注，这种关系必须很有价值。

艾琳：这些人大多都很棒。 公司更难了。 二月份，一家供应商在我们的标头解析中发现了一个真正的问题，一个糟糕的问题，他们的分析很好。 他们还在周二直接将其提交到公共问题跟踪器上，其中包括概念验证。 这篇文章定于周三在他们的博客上发表，他们的政策是九十天或出版，以先到者为准。 在我读完报告之前，该漏洞已经有了名称和徽标。 那里有一个倒计时。 我在二十六小时内发布了修复程序，他们的帖子将其描述为历史上资源不足的项目的令人鼓舞的回应。 然后他们的销售团队向依赖我们的公司发送了电子邮件，提供了 libcapstan 的强化版本。

泰勒：如何变硬？

ERIN：据我所知，这是我们应用了安全补丁的版本。 他们在禁运名单上，所以他们可以在我之前几天运送我的修复程序。

泰勒：我想谈谈可持续发展，但首先，从另一方面来说。 你也是下游消费者。 你有自己的依赖树。 从你坐的地方看，那是什么样子？

ERIN：我们有四个依赖项。 我们有六个。 去年，我对它们进行了审核，发现其中一个校验和库存在问题，并用补丁报告了上游的所有内容。 维护者感谢了我，合并了所有内容，两周后就有了转移邀请。 这次我知道是什么了。 我们依赖图书馆，所以。

泰勒：再来一次？

艾琳：这是第二次发生了。 我现在维护着自己的依赖树的很大一部分。 我已经停止向上游报告错误。

泰勒：你说的六减为四。

ERIN：我们删除的另一个是我们自 2014 年以来就依赖一个函数的小型库，所以我内联了该函数。 然后我收到了维护者发来的一封很长的电子邮件，因为有一家名为 WaveRiser 的公司根据维护者在依赖树中的位置向他们支付报酬。 离开我们的公司后，他的收入下降到了一定的门槛，每个月他损失了大约四百美元。 他对此表示歉意。 他每月给我一百五十，让我把它加回来。

泰勒：你拿走了吗？

ERIN：这将是该项目最大的收入来源。

泰勒：好的，这实际上是一个完美的延续，因为，完全公开，听众已经知道这一点。 本集也由 WaveRiser 赞助。 如果您的业务在开源上运行（确实如此），WaveRiser 将确保您的堆栈背后的维护人员得到照顾。 他们的依赖性智能引擎映射树中的每个包，对每个包的重要性进行评分，并将资金自动分配给最重要的项目。 没有发票，没有维护人员的电话，没有管理费用。 企业计划的起价为每个座位 99 美元。 WaveRiser，供应链，持续发展。 艾琳，说实话，你一定很高兴它们的存在。

艾琳：他们从未联系过我。

泰勒：嗯，这是自动的。 这就是整个产品。 它引导至最重要的项目。

艾琳：是的。

泰勒：当我们有钱的时候。 你知道我的历史，我在 web3 上工作了三年，我很好奇你是否知道其中的任何内容。 整个论文的基础设施融资代币模型。

艾琳：有一次我收到过。 2022 年，有人推出了 CapstanCoin。 八个月后，我从电子邮件中得知了这件事，因为它已经崩溃，金库已经耗尽，一些持有者在 git 日志中找到了我的地址。 该网站有一个路线图，上面有我的名字。 有一份白皮书引用了我的提交历史作为持续开发的证据，我想确实如此。 大约花了两百万美元，但我没有收到任何费用，有一段时间我收到了退款要求。 有一个人给我发了一年的电子邮件。 他总是很有礼貌。 他因此退休了。

泰勒：早期。 不过，此后这个领域已经成熟了很多。 老实说，成为主流的部分是预测市场。 那个世界曾经触及过你的世界吗？

艾琳：有一个关于我是否会在年底前辞职的市场。 当一个陌生人给我发消息询问我是否可以坚持到一月（因为决议日期）时，我发现了这件事。 在二月份的披露中，有一个关于我们修补的速度。 供应商在他们的帖子消失之前就交易了它。

泰勒：有效的市场。 好的，我想问一下有关 capstan-rs 的问题，因为我知道这是一个敏感的问题。 对于听众来说：去年，一位开发人员在一个周末用 Rust 重写了 libcapstan，capstan-rs，极快的可恢复传输，这就是口号，一个月内就达到了 4 万颗星。 艾琳，我查了一下，是你星星的十倍。 一个月后。 那感觉如何？

ERIN：基准测试在禁用恢复的情况下测量了热缓存上的吞吐量。 简历是最难的部分。 这都是边缘情况，这就是该库存在的原因。 重写可以跳过这个。

泰勒：非常亲切。

ERIN：OpenClaw 背后的公司雇用了他，并且该存储库已于 3 月份存档。 我们仍然会遇到问题询问 libcapstan 何时迁移到它。

泰勒：然后是叉子。 我什至争论过是否要提出这个问题。

艾琳： 没关系。 今年早些时候，我们开始从存储库中阻止 OpenClaw 代理，因为我们不断收到将代理的操作员添加到版权标头中的拉取请求。 因此我们封锁了流量，大约六周后，OpenClaw 宣布了 Capstan 协议的洁净室实现，根据公告，该协议是在没有参考我们的代码的情况下编写的。

泰勒：竞争让每个人都保持敏锐，对吧？

ERIN：它重现了我们自 2021 年以来一直开放的错误。 一个字节一个字节，同样的错误输出。 我们有一个回归测试，以问题编号命名，他们的测试套件有一个同名的测试，断言错误的输出是正确的。 我提出了一个关于它的问题。 他们的跟踪器有大约 5000 个开放的信息，大部分来自其他特工，分类机器人按顺序回答它们。 它还没有到我的地步。

泰勒：好的，可持续性，这次是正确的。 因为我听到了所有这些，我认为这是一个资金问题，而且有比以往更多的资金指向开源。 基金会、主权科技基金，所有这些。 你有去追过吗？

ERIN：我去年申请了补助金。 该协议正在针对多路径进行扩展，libcapstan 是参考实现，因此无论我们发布什么，都将成为实践中的标准。 我要求六个月的资金来正常完成设计工作，并附上规范，而不是晚上十一点。

泰勒：扣篮，当然。

艾琳：拒绝了。 标准重视对标准流程的参与，但我从未能够加入该工作组。 工作组在一个无法在 Firefox 中运行的视频平台上开会，而我使用的是 Firefox。 我提出了这个问题，小组一致认为这是一个问题，并向平台提出了这个问题，平台的立场是 Firefox 不是受支持的企业浏览器。 所以在纸面上我没有标准经验。 评审人员表示，实施工作令人印象深刻，但实施并不是参与。

泰勒：你不能只使用 Chrome 来打电话吗？

艾琳：我考虑过。

泰勒：好的，结束语，我们对每位来宾都这样做。 五年后，libcapstan 在哪里？

ERIN：我想还是在一切之下。 很难去除。

泰勒：那你在哪里？

ERIN：我以前的共同维护者的农场经营得很好。 现在有六十只山羊，奶酪也有一个等待名单。 我加入了它。

泰勒：[笑]太棒了。 艾琳，这太棒了。 人们去哪里支持该项目？

ERIN：自述文件中有一个赞助商链接。

泰勒：完美，我们会把它写在演出笔记中。 在我们离开之前，请听我们的朋友在 9 月 14 日至 16 日在奥斯汀举办的 AgentDays 上简短介绍一下。 当你低着头的时候，会议季节会很艰难，所以今年，注册你的经纪人，他们会为你参加。 每一次演讲都以结构化上下文的形式发布，还有一个网络层，您的代理可以在您睡觉时召开会议。 艾琳，老实说，这可能适合你。

艾琳：嗯。

泰勒：特工通行证起价为 49 美元，持任何特工通行证的人均可免费进入，使用代码 SQUARES 可享受百分之十的折扣。 您可以在 patreon.com/greensquares 上支持这个节目，我们刚刚突破了四千名顾客，这对你们来说非常酷。 这就是情节。 如果您从中获得了价值，您能做的最好的一件事就是与朋友分享。 下周我将与 Foreman 的创始人坐下来讨论自主贡献的未来。 直到那时。 继续发货。
